name: line-chart
title: Line Chart
description: A smooth line chart that draws itself in; drag across it and a guide, a dot and a label follow the finger.

perf.budget: The curve is built once per data change; drawing in, scrubbing and three pulses of the latest point are shared values read by one Skia canvas. Nothing is drawn at rest.

measurements.notes: Pulses three times after drawing in, then draws nothing at rest (0 frames in 5 s). It used to pulse forever.

a11y.reducedMotion: The line appears complete, without drawing in, and the latest point does not pulse.
a11y.screenReader: Adjustable: swipe up and down to step through the points; each reads its label and value.
a11y.touchTarget: The whole chart is the scrub area.

meta.guide:
## Usage

```tsx
import { LineChart } from '@/components/kinetik/line-chart';

<LineChart
  accessibilityLabel="Revenue, last 12 months"
  data={revenue}
  labels={months}
  formatValue={(v) => `$${(v / 1000).toFixed(1)}k`}
  onScrub={(i) => setFocus(i)}
/>;
```

The chart fills its parent's width. The curve passes through every value without overshooting, so a dip never draws below its real number. `onScrub` reports the index under the finger (and `null` when it lifts), which is handy for a headline figure above the chart.

## When to use

- Trends over time: revenue, steps, heart rate, prices.
- Dashboards where people want to read the exact value at a moment.

## When not to use

- Comparing separate categories. Use Bar Chart.
- Dense data with thousands of points; down-sample first.

## Notes

- The line draws in whenever the data changes, with the area revealed behind it.
- The latest point pulses a few times after the line draws in, a quiet "this is live", then rests so a chart on screen costs no frames.
- Screen readers step through the points with the adjustable increment and decrement actions.

docs: Prefer `npx kinetik-ui add line-chart`: it installs dependencies with expo install, so versions match your Expo SDK.
